record.title: Project discovery can select state from a shared ancestor directory
record.description: `findStateFiles` searches from the hook's working directory to the filesystem root and accepts the first ancestor `.stilo/state.json`. If a lower-privileged principal can create that file in a shared ancestor, a session without a nearer state file may use the planted state and checkpoint. The state fields then affect injected project and phase context; malformed state can instead trigger directives to stop and repair it. Source confirms the path and propagation, but this run did not establish whether an attacker can write to a relevant ancestor or observe the resulting host/model behavior.
record.claimed_root_cause: `hooks/stilo-state.js#findStateFiles` stops only at the filesystem root and has no configured ceiling or ownership check. `resolveProjeto` uses the first matching path. The resulting state path also determines the checkpoint path.

trace.description: Resolves the project from the hook working directory. SubagentStart and UserPromptSubmit also call project resolution.
Walks upward until the filesystem root, returning the first existing ancestor `.stilo/state.json`.
Passes the discovered paths to the resolver, which reads and validates the sole match.
Derives `.stilo/checkpoint.json` from the selected state path; checkpoint text is included in the state context.
Renders validated project and phase fields; unreadable or invalid state produces repair or stop directives.
Writes assembled context to stdout for the host to consume.

evidence.description: `findStateFiles` accepts only a cwd argument and defines no search ceiling or ownership check.
The first existing ancestor state path is returned.
The upward walk ends only when the parent equals the current path.
Checkpoint location is derived from the selected state path.
Unreadable state produces a repeated instruction not to create or restart the project and to repair the file.
The ruleset directs the agent to write phase transitions to the discovered state file.
The test verifies that upward search takes precedence over a nested project; it does not test a ceiling above the workspace or home directory.

blockers: Whether a different, lower-privileged principal can create `.stilo/state.json` in an ancestor of a relevant working directory depends on that host's filesystem permissions and sharing configuration; this is not established by repository source.
This host has no OS-enforced sandbox, so the hook was not run and injection from a planted ancestor state was not observed.
Whether Claude Code or Codex and the model act on the injected state or checkpoint text is runtime behavior not established by source.

validation_plan.local: In an approved OS-enforced sandbox with networking disabled, a throwaway root, read-only target, empty allowlisted environment, and bounded resources, create a valid state and checkpoint at the sandbox root and a victim project beneath it with no local `.stilo` directory. Call `resolveProjeto` and the context builder; record whether the ancestor path is selected and its state/checkpoint values appear in the context. Repeat with an unreadable state file. Do not run this check if the required sandbox controls are unavailable.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a disposable host/profile: inspect permissions on relevant shared ancestors and determine whether a separate standard account can create `.stilo/state.json` there. If so, use a throwaway project with harmless state/checkpoint values and record whether SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, or SubagentStart selects and injects them. Do not use a production project or sensitive content.
